# Best portable power stations for camping

The right size depends on your trip. The 250-500Wh class is the sweet spot for tent and car camping, and the bigger units suit multi-day trips with a fridge or cooler.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 270-290Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249): The top pick in PowerStationGearLab's guide. It has 288Wh, weighs 8.3 lb, and has a 300W output. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2 (faster recharging, shorter warranty), but the Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299): The same capacity (286Wh) with a 600W inverter, and it can expand to 572Wh.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199): Has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the AC-less "DC" variant.
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179): The budget pick, with 268Wh and a 600W inverter.

Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). They earn affiliate commissions, and their own ratings favor these units. OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the Jackery 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low overall, though it recommends the Jackery 300 for phones and laptops.

## Multi-day trips, a 12V fridge, or van and overland use
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (under ~$900 on sale, $1,499 list): OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping, tied for the highest score of 14 units tested. It weighs 39 lb and delivers 2,200W. It recharges fully in about 2.5 hours and is easy to pair with solar panels. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799): A step-down option with 1,070Wh and 1,500W. TechRadar also lists it as its best for camping. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** ($1,079 on sale): WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65-rated and shock-proof, with 1,536Wh. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Mid-range value
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (under ~$530 on sale): OutdoorGearLab's best value. It's compact with plenty of ports, but its fan is noisy and capacity is limited. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti AC180** ($499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF): 1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 35 lb (16 kg), with a 5-year warranty. It suits weekend trips and power tools. Dealectric tested the code in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. The link below is an affiliate link, so the retailer pays Dealectric a commission at no cost to you. ## Quick tips
- A CPAP uses roughly 30-60Wh per night with the humidifier off. A 288Wh unit can run most for 3-5 nights.
- These units are too large for planes (100Wh airline limit), so they're for car and campsite use.
- Black Friday is coming, and TechRadar notes it's a good time to shop for these.

The search results didn't include direct retailer links for most of these models. The review pages above have the current price links, or you can search the exact model name on Amazon or the brand's site.

If you tell me what you'll run (fridge, CPAP, laptop) and how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
